newsitem.title: UK: Ockham says to float Wise Speke business.
newsitem.headline: Ockham says to float Wise Speke business.

text.p: Lloyd's insurance group Ockham Holdings said on Monday it was to float its wholly-owned stockbroking subsidiary Wise Speke.

The decision to list Wise Speke on the stock exchange follows other restructuring at Ockham, designed to move the company towards direct involvement in retail insurance and other financial services, and away from its pure Lloyd's managing agency role.
"It has been our strategic aim to achieve this change for the benefit of Ockham's shareholders; we are now well on the way to turnaround," said Ockham chief executive David Poole.
The listing will be achieved through a placing of part of Ockham's holding of existing ordinary shares. In addition, a placing of new shares is expected to raise three million stg.
After the listing, due to happen later this year, Ockham will retain a 60 percent interest in Wise Speke and continue to consolidate the stockbroker's results in its accounts.

A prospectus forecasts that pretax pre-exceptional profits for Wise Speke this year will be 2.25 million stg. Ockham's profit and loss account will record a net loss on disposal, with gains from the float credited to reserves.

Ockham earlier this month sold its aviation and non-marine underwriting operations to Bermudan catastrophe insurer ACE, and secured a cash injection of over 20 million stg for its motor business Highway.

These moves demonstrated how Ockham is trying to re-invent itself following losses in the Lloyd's of London market from 1988 to 1992 estimated at over one billion stg and how, with the market back in profit and its future secured, corporate investors are aligning more closely with underwriting.
